title: Where should the tea stall stand for two friends?
description: Two friends live on one long straight village road, and a tea stall is to open at the spot where they meet. The board shows the two gates and an empty marked place, and stops on the question of where the stall should stand.
teaching_notes: One idea: a fair meeting spot between two places is the same walk from each. Ask each child to guess a spot and give a reason, and do not confirm any guess, because the lessons that follow settle it. Watch for students who pick a spot only because it looks near the middle.

source: The mean of two numbers sits halfway
video_script.why: Before any word of mean, the child meets the real question: where is the fair spot between two places on a line.
video_script.substitution: Picture the road as a straight line with two gates on it and a spot between them that is the same walk from both.
video_script.anchor: a long straight village road with a gate near each end and a tea stall waiting to be set down at the meeting spot
never_show: the exact spot of the stall
maths_rules: The road is a straight line with one gate on the left and one gate on the right, with a clear gap between them.
The stall spot is shown only as an empty marked place, never placed on the line.
No distances or numbers are drawn.
The open question: where must the stall stand so that both friends walk the same distance. The answer is never shown or hinted.
video_script.design: One idea: a fair spot between two gates is the same walk from each. Assumes nothing. No wrong idea is broken. The road and the two gates stay to the end.
